messages:
anna: Heads up — apiserver 503s in ap-southeast1 starting ~14:08 UTC. Coincident with a big GPU attach/onboard burst from the provisioner. Seeing leader heartbeat jitter and controller-manager lease renew errors. Logs show repeated 503s and watch reconnects.

sre-oncall: On it. Pulling etcd leader metrics + WAL latency now. Any short term mitigations proposed?

mike: Grafana: etcd leader CPU spiked ~3x, nvme iops up, and CP-plane egress to GPU hosts is ~95% saturated. NAT/SNAT metrics show conntrack saturating.

julia: Looks like the GPU provisioner is hitting all AZs and flooding NAT gateways with attach flows. Conntrack churn will make apiserver proxies fail fast.

rahul: Confirmed from controller-manager logs: lease renew failed repeatedly -> `error renewing lease: timed out`. Also `apiserver: 503` bubbled up to kubelets.

anna: Quick mitigation rolling: reduce GPU onboard parallelism and pause autoscale for the provisioner for 20m. Patch applied: `kubectl patch job gpu-onboard -p '{"spec":{"parallelism":2}}'`

deploy-bot: Patch applied by anna to job/gpu-onboard (sha: abc123) — rollout complete.

mike: Also going to bump conntrack as a stopgap on NAT boxes: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` and monitor.

julia: Can we short-circuit user traffic to a CPU-variant / fallback model route to avoid client-facing 503s? We have route rules for model fallback.

rahul: That helps UX. For control plane health we should also reduce controller-manager reconcile rate temporarily: set `--horizontal-pod-autoscaler-sync-period=30s`? Maybe I mean controllers' resync? We can add rate-limiter config to reduce stormy reconciles.

anna: Implementing two-prong: 1) throttle provisioning (done) 2) enable fallback model route for serving traffic (starting now) 3) conntrack bump on nat (mike).

mike: Note: long-term fix is reserved GPU headroom in ap-southeast1 (extra Dedicated pool) so attach storms can't saturate shared NAT. Cost estimate: ~6k/day for the short window if we spin up immediate capacity. Ops to approve?

julia: ops said temporary weekend spend is OK if it prevents customer impact — propose 6hr runway, then revert. :thumbsup:

rahul: Additional metric: `etcd_disk_wal_fsync_duration_seconds` jumped >500ms during the spike, which explains leader CPU and election jitter. We should avoid WAL thrash from multi-host attach IO spikes.

anna: Filing incident ticket & timeline: https://incidents/redwood/75299 — I'll update once 503s are down. @sre-oncall keep a 15m cadence check.

sre-oncall: Monitoring apiserver 5xx rate, etcd fsync and conntrack. Early signs: 503s trending down since throttles and patch. Will confirm in 10m.

mike: If we see recurring daily bursts, we should throttle onboard job at source (CI/ML team) and add provisioning circuit-breaker on the provisioner side.

julia: Agreed. Also add alerting rule for nat_conntrack_utilization > 80% + etcd_wal_fsync > 200ms combined.

anna: Thanks all. Next steps: keep throttled, observe 30m, consider temporary dedicated headroom if not stable.

rahul: 👍 Also will draft a short runbook for this failure mode (GPU attach -> NAT saturation -> etcd WAL thrash -> apiserver 503s).

anna: Closing loop soon with postmortem stub. Thanks team. 🙏
